notes: **Mathematical (classical) probability:** $P(E) = \frac{\text{number of favourable outcomes}}{\text{total number of equally likely outcomes}}$. Assumes all outcomes are equally likely.
**Empirical (statistical) probability:** $P(E) = \frac{\text{number of times event occurs}}{\text{total number of trials}}$. Based on observed frequency.
**Independent cases:** two events are independent if occurrence of one does not affect probability of the other. $P(A \cap B) = P(A) \times P(B)$ for independent events.
**Addition law:** $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)$. For mutually exclusive events ($A \cap B = \emptyset$): $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B)$.
**Multiplication law:** $P(A \cap B) = P(A) \times P(B|A)$. For independent events: $P(B|A) = P(B)$, so $P(A \cap B) = P(A)P(B)$.
